chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hammid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "He has lied who claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something, or in something, or on something."
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about God being in or from something?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the doctrine of divine transcendence (Tanzih) by negating both spatial containment ('in') and physical derivation ('from'), while also rejecting the anthropomorphic notion of God being 'on' a throne as a physical entity. This narration is pivotal in Shia kalam for distinguishing between the metaphorical 'Istawa' (rising over) the Throne and literal physical location, affirming that God is free from the limitations of created matter. It reinforces the concept that divine essence is not subject to the categories of place or direction.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. And with this chain of transmission, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of Hammid
that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: “Whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something, in something, or on something, has surely lied.”
